newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lauds U.S. ban on gun sales to Paraguay.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lauds U.S. ban on gun sales to Paraguay.

text.p: The Brazilian government on Thursday lauded a decision by Washington to ban gun sales to Paraguay, saying the measure would significantly reduce the flow of contraband arms into Latin America's largest country.
Justice Minister Nelson Jobim said in a statement that the U.S. move was a "vital" measure for Brazil's battle against violence.
"We're not hitting the criminal himself but it's the start of the destruction of the intruments that allow violence to take place," he said.

The U.S. embassy in Brasilia announced on Wednesday that the State Department had suspended all licenses for the export of firearms, rifles, components and ammunition to Paraguay, exempting only some hunting rifles.
Brazil has long complained that most of the illegal weapons used by criminals are smuggled in from neighbouring Paraguay, a charge that Asuncion denies.

The Brazilian Justice Ministry's statement acknowledged that any estimate of the numbers of weapons smuggled over the border was just "speculation". But it added there were indications that 70 percent of those weapons originated in the United States.

It said Colombia was another route for gun-smugglers and that talks were underway on how to cooperate in the fight against the trade and also against drug-smuggling, which frequently went hand-in-hand.

In a move to curb a rising tide of violence, the lower house of the Brazilian Congress voted earlier this month to make the illegal carrying of firearms a criminal offence. The bill now faces a vote in the Senate.
